title: Accept a Higher Power
coreMove: Accept a higher power by doing the next honest task, naming what you cannot command, asking for wisdom, and letting the result stop pretending to be yours.

exampleSpecs.domain: adult learning class on recovery language
exampleSpecs.audience: readers who hear surrender as giving up
exampleSpecs.stakes: confusing help with defeat can keep denial in charge
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A learner works through why Alcoholics Anonymous begins with powerlessness.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers trying to control outcomes through more checking
exampleSpecs.stakes: a worry list can become a false claim of control
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A page turns worry into three named jobs without a two-panel scaffold.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers learning to spot false self-command
exampleSpecs.stakes: control may sound responsible while it rejects the help it needs
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two people use recovery language to name the sentence that keeps help outside.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose control habit sounds responsible inside their head
exampleSpecs.stakes: a private loop can keep stealing care from the task that remains
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Thought by thought, Rosaire catches the false link between care and control.

exampleSpecs.audience: people who let urgent worries outrank needed support
exampleSpecs.stakes: pressure can make help look optional right when it is the structure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: A peer reframes the meeting as the support that lets the other tasks happen cleanly.

exampleSpecs.domain: public hearing statement under time pressure
exampleSpecs.audience: readers facing outcomes they can influence but not command
exampleSpecs.stakes: two bad options can make control look like care
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Kevin uses the serenity prayer to choose the action he owns and release the vote.
